verdict: PASS — v0.6.3 cut in all four repositories, proved on a blank Ubuntu host against the released artefacts, and deployed to the beta instance (core 125 -> 144, search 16 -> 18)
section: v0.6.3 release — cut, verified, deployed to beta — 2026-09-09
headline: deploy/release.sh --yes v0.6.3 tagged the meta repository and cut a GitHub release in each of the three component repositories, each release's publish-container run pushed and verified its GHCR image, and the frozen candidate manifest resolved four source SHAs, three OCI index digests, three release assets and their SHA256SUMS entries with the contract and generated-type checks green. The A02 blank-server harness passed against those exact artefacts on a fresh Ubuntu 24.04 VM; the A03 runtime harness reached a clean first-deploy core 144 / search 18 ledger and both dirty-ledger aborts, and could not certify the frontend because Node 26 under Ubuntu's qemu-user-static segfaults on this arm64 lab host. The beta instance, real amd64, upgraded 125 -> 144 and 16 -> 18 in 54 seconds with deploy/deploy.sh unmodified and every probe green.

not_certified_here.frontend_probe: deploy.sh's 6/6 frontend probe timed out at 300s. Cause measured, and it is the emulator, not the release: the container logs only 'x86_64-binfmt-P: QEMU internal SIGSEGV {code=MAPERR, addr=0x20}' in a crash loop. The IDENTICAL image digest serves HTTP 200 in 6s under Docker Desktop's emulation on the same workstation (Next.js 16.3.0, 54247 bytes), and serves the beta instance natively on amd64. v0.6.2's frontend (Node 24) did not crash under this emulator on 2026-09-05; v0.6.3's is Node 26.
not_certified_here.internal_tls_transition: the harness reaches it only after the plain-http deploy returns 0, so the selected internal-CA TLS mode was not re-proved for v0.6.3. It passed for v0.6.2 on 2026-09-05. The real ACME edge is proved on beta below.

harness_defects_found_and_fixed: tests/runtime_smoke.py pinned the release digests with a regex anchored on a literal 'ghcr.io/', which stopped matching when VIDRA_IMAGE_REGISTRY made the registry host interpolated. Zero matches for all three repositories; the require(count > 0) guard turned that into a refusal instead of a run that silently tested the mutable tag. Fixed to match any '<prefix>/<repo>:'.

The same platform pin did not extend to clamav, which the scan-by-default profile set now starts and which is published for linux/amd64 only — so compose pull died with 'no matching manifest for linux/arm64/v8' before anything started. Fixed by stamping the candidate's platform onto the clamav service in the disposable bundle copy. Measured affordable first: clamd healthy in 81s at 996 MiB RSS under emulation, inside its own 120s start_period.

The undo is the restore path: ./deploy/restore.sh backups/pre-deploy-2026-09-09T212458.dump.gz with VIDRA_*_TAG back at v0.6.2 — restore.sh refuses a dirty dump and refuses a pinned image whose schema is below the dump's, both before the drop.

scan_posture.decision: MALWARE_SCAN_MODE=disabled — the documented opt-out. The scan profile was NOT enabled on beta.
scan_posture.why: the droplet's env file (the operator's file, not the template) carried MALWARE_SCAN_ENABLED=false, no CLAMAV_ADDR and VIDRA_COMPOSE_PROFILES='core frontend'. Under v0.6.3 that pair is not a posture: MALWARE_SCAN_ENABLED is no longer read, and with neither an address nor the opt-out the api boots and refuses EVERY ingestion route with 503 scanner_not_configured. Leaving it would have silently broken uploads on beta.
scan_posture.ram_check: free -m showed 7941 MiB total with 6720 available, so clamd's ~2 GiB would have fitted. It was still declined: beta has never scanned, and adding a new service the api waits on service_healthy (120s start_period, first-boot freshclam) inside a 19-migration upgrade lengthens the restart window for a capability the instance did not have. The opt-out is a first-class posture: the api WARNs every boot, writes one system.malware_scan.disabled audit row per boot, and /admin/system reports clamav not_configured.
scan_posture.verified: GET /api/v1/instance reports features.uploads=true and features.imports=true, so ingestion is allowed rather than refused

doctor.cli_note: the droplet's /usr/local/bin/vidra was an August build. deploy.sh upgrades images, never the CLI, so the first `vidra doctor` after the upgrade reported two FALSE failures: it rejected MALWARE_SCAN_MODE=disabled as 'must be one of fail-closed, fail-open, quarantine' (a mode the running api had accepted at boot) and could not read the schema ledger ('exec: "migrate": executable file not found in $PATH' — the defect core #191 fixed). The CLI was reinstalled at v0.6.3 from the release asset, verified against the release SHA256SUMS (859a7b5e...), with the old binary kept at /root/vidra-cli.bak-preupgrade.
doctor.the_one_failure: domain DNS — the hostname resolves to Cloudflare, not to this host. Expected and known; it is the same fact VIDRA_SKIP_DNS_PREFLIGHT exists for, and it is why ACME renewal on this instance is a standing risk.
notable_warnings: instance owner: NO account is marked as this instance's owner. Migration 0131's marker is written only by the first-run setup claim, and this instance was claimed before it existed; the backfill needs an auth.owner_claim audit row or a claimed owner_claim_tokens row whose claimed_at matches the founding account's created_at, and neither survived here. Nothing is broken (the last-admin guard still holds) but every admin is equal.
bucket ownership: the media bucket carries no .vidra/owner marker, so media GC would report what it would delete and delete nothing
